title: On the web, connecting ChatGPT Codex shows a code to type on OpenAI's device page instead of asking for a localhost address; the desktop app keeps the browser sign-in
steps: S1: run the tracy-web seat-plan broker, route and Codex vendor tests (node:test, TEST_DATABASE_URL = the stand's Postgres, fake vendor fetch) and the tracy-model-plan connect tests.

S2: the end-to-end form: on cowork.tracy.site, Settings > AI accounts > ChatGPT Codex > Connect now; the panel shows a code, Copy code and Open ChatGPT Codex (https://auth.openai.com/codex/device); typing the code there connects the account without pasting an address. In the desktop app the same press opens the browser sign-in and the app catches the callback.
expect: POST /api/seat-plan/connect/start {provider: 'codex', surface: 'web'} (or no surface) answers signIn 'device' with userCode and authorizeUrl https://auth.openai.com/codex/device, and never the device code itself.
The same start with surface 'desktop' answers signIn 'browser' with an authorizeUrl whose redirect_uri is http://localhost:1455/auth/callback.
Claude starts a browser sign-in on every surface; GitHub Copilot a device sign-in on every surface.
An attempt finishes the way it started: a pasted address for a device attempt, or a poll for a browser one, is refused 400 invalid and the attempt stays open.
The page sends surface 'desktop' when window.tracyDesktop exists, else 'web'; the device panel shows OpenAI's page and the code the broker sent.
GET /api/seat-plan/status lists webSignIn per provider: codex 'device', claude 'browser', copilot 'device', key vendors 'key'.

tests: on the web Codex hands back a code to type; on the desktop it opens the browser sign-in
Claude opens the browser sign-in on both surfaces, Copilot a device code on both
a Codex device attempt connects once OpenAI confirms
a Codex attempt finishes the way it started, whatever the vendor offers elsewhere
status says how each vendor signs in
connect/start hands the broker the surface the person signs in from; anything else is the web
on the web Codex signs in with a device code, on the desktop through the browser
device sign-in starts with OpenAI and hands back the code the person types
device poll stays pending while OpenAI answers 403 or 404
a confirmed device code is exchanged for tokens through the device callback
the start says which surface signs in: the desktop app when the page runs in it, else the web
a Codex device sign-in shows OpenAI's page and the code the broker sent, nothing of GitHub

fence: the sign-in kind is chosen once at connect/start from the vendor and the surface, sealed in the attempt, and complete() finishes it that way; the vendors' registered redirect URIs are unchanged
